title: Wire sparse-elim emitter for GF(2) and GF(p)
description: Extend `crates/gf2-coding/examples/bench_sparse_csv_emitter.rs` to emit `sparse-elim,GF(2)` and `sparse-elim,GF(p)` rows for each prime in `{7, 251, 65521, 2^31-1}`. Closes the 10 sparse-elim PENDING rows in `dev/bench_results/2026-05-04-47698404-sparse-tables.md` left by the 47698404 scorecard. ## Background 47698404's bench emitter currently wires sparse-elim ONLY for GF(2^m) (gated behind `--full`). The GF(2) elim path via `SpBitMatrixDual` does not have a public `rref()` exposed and the GF(p) path via `SparseFieldMatrix::>::rref()` (`crates/gf2-core/src/field/sparse_matrix.rs:1257`) is not called from the emitter. LinBox numbers for these cells are already in `dev/bench_results/2026-05-04-47698404-sparse-reference.csv:11-24`, awaiting the gf2-side companion. Per scorecard § 5 #3, this is a `not-yet-harnessed` marker per protocol § 9 Amendment 2. ## Naming convention note (lead-clarification, 2026-05-05) The CSV operation key is `sparse-elim` (matches existing GF(2^m) emitter rows and protocol § 7 schema). ## Success Criteria - [hard] `bench_sparse_csv_emitter.rs --quick` emits `sparse-elim,GF(2)` rows at n ∈ {256, 1024} matching the LinBox reference shape (from `linbox_sparse_bench.cpp:248-272`). - [hard] `bench_sparse_csv_emitter.rs --quick` emits `sparse-elim,GF(p)` rows for each prime in {GF(7), GF(251), GF(65521), GF(2^31-1)} at n ∈ {256, 1024}. - [hard] If `SpBitMatrixDual::rref` (or equivalent GF(2) sparse RREF entry-point) is missing, add it as part of this task with doctests. - [hard] After regenerating `2026-05-04-47698404-sparse.csv` and `2026-05-04-47698404-sparse-tables.md`, all 10 sparse-elim gf2-side PENDING entries clear. - [hard] Smoke at n=16 for sparse-elim cells extends `benchmarks/reference/sparse_smoke.cpp` per protocol § 6. Baseline: an in-harness scalar Gauss-Jordan reference (`scalar_rref` in `sparse_smoke.cpp`) compared against LinBox `GaussDomain::NoReordering`; the gf2-core sparse RREF candidates (`SpBitMatrix::rref`, `SparseFieldMatrix::rref`) are independently cross-checked against the dense `gf2_core::alg::rref::rref` reference in Rust tests (`crates/gf2-core/src/sparse.rs::tests::*rref*`). Together these give the multi-witness coverage protocol § 6 calls for. Upgrade to direct C++-side gf2-core integration is tracked by 96fde7c7 (same systemic 96fde7c7 dependency as 47698404 / b13799ac / 9a715d75); until that lands, the scalar/LinBox + dense-Rust-reference branch is the active deliverable per protocol § 9 Amendment 2 (`not-yet-harnessed` marker). - [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, `doc-review` pass. ## References - 47698404 scorecard § 5 #3: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-04-47698404-sparse-scorecard.md` - Existing GF(2^m) elim wiring: `bench_sparse_csv_emitter.rs:715-744` (gated behind `--full`) - GF(p) RREF method: `crates/gf2-core/src/field/sparse_matrix.rs:1257` - LinBox reference rows: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-04-47698404-sparse-reference.csv:11-24` - Sibling: 521390db (parallel scalar-reference + 96fde7c7 amendment for sparse×dense × GF(2)). - Upstream design for direct gf2-core smoke integration: 96fde7c7.
